questions.question: 94 guide features are typed as genes in the matrix. Keep them out of the gene expression before normalising?
questions.why_it_matters: counted as genes they enter every DE test

questions.question: The feature reference labels 12 guides 'Non-Targeting' (e.g. NTC-6-i, NTC-1-i, NTC-2-i). Are they the controls, and of which kind: non-targeting, or cutting (safe-targeting, intergenic)? Is any labelled target a control too (a gene-targeting negative control)?
questions.why_it_matters: the reference and every hidden check are built from the controls

questions.question: Are the 6 captures (barcode prefixes of one matrix) independent replicates (mice, donors, separate cultures) or technical splits of one pool (lanes, wells)?
questions.why_it_matters: each result's n names the biological replicates (mice, donors) apart from technical ones (lanes, wells)

questions.question: With these captures (barcode prefixes of one matrix), pseudobulk can test 21% of the targets. Are there other samples (hashtag replicates, donors) the files do not show?
questions.why_it_matters: pseudobulk by sample needs 3 samples that hold both the target's and the control cells

questions.question: S1Sa_ captured guides poorly (few guide UMIs per cell, or a small share on each cell's top guide). Keep their cells, or treat their guide calls as unreliable?
questions.why_it_matters: a weak guide library makes callers call ambient guides

questions.question: The cell metadata hold perturbation labels derived from the guides (column 'guide_group2'). Use the deposit's labels as the perturbation unit, after checking them against the guide calls?
questions.why_it_matters: re-deriving labels from guide names is where parsing mistakes happen

questions.question: The samples split in two expression groups ({1: ['S1Sa_', 'S2Sp_'], 2: ['D1_', 'D2_', 'D3_', 'S3SaSp_']}). Are these conditions?
questions.why_it_matters: pooling conditions mixes their effects; one screen per condition

questions.question: 69 guides appear in only some captures (barcode prefixes of one matrix) (e.g. ARID1A-a1 in 1 of 3). If any are controls, which units lack a matched reference, and do the units differ otherwise (stage, condition)?
questions.why_it_matters: a sample without control cells is compared with all other perturbed cells, and the report says so

questions.question: Cells per control guide vary 3.4-fold. Is the library's representation (plasmid or early counts) available?
questions.why_it_matters: without it, cell numbers cannot be read as fitness

questions.question: 14 of 53 pairs have no captures (barcode prefixes of one matrix) that holds both of their singles (e.g. BTF3-i|KLF1-i). Leave them out of interaction tests, or compare across units?
questions.why_it_matters: an interaction is a claim about three groups in one replicate

questions.question: Some factors cannot be separated across units (e.g. library = pairs only under batch = batch2). Compare within the shared level, or relative to other targets?
questions.why_it_matters: a batch confounded with a condition or library looks like an effect

questions.question: Were cells of another population pooled into any sample before sequencing (wild-type cells, a spike-in line, another genotype)? The methods usually say; a marker gene per group can confirm it.
questions.why_it_matters: a pooled-in population sits silently inside groups

questions.question: Does the analysis depend on data outside this deposit (a reference screen, a gene list, a paper's table)? List them before planning.
questions.why_it_matters: an outside dependency missing from the plan blocks a whole question

questions.question: Confirm the modality: knockout, CRISPRi, CRISPRa, base editing, or mixed (guides of different modes in one library: then each guide's mode, in perturbation.guides).
